Title: Out-of-bounds read in scan_buffer::iterator::operator++
Analysis:
In `test/scan.h`, `scan_buffer::iterator::operator++` contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability. Specifically, when `buf_->try_consume()` returns `false`, indicating that the end of the input buffer has been reached and `buf_->ptr_` has been advanced to `buf_->end_`, the function still unconditionally dereferences `buf_->ptr_` on line 97: `value_ = *buf_->ptr_;`. Since `buf_->ptr_` points to the memory location immediately following the valid buffer data (`buf_->end_`), this results in an out-of-bounds read of one-past-the-end of the buffer.

### Conceptual Exploit Payload

An application calls `fmt::scan` to parse user input, for example:
```cpp
std::string input = "foo";
fmt::scan(input, "foo");
```

During parsing, the iterator advances through `"foo"` character-by-character. When incrementing past the last character:
1. `try_consume()` is called, incrementing `ptr_` to equal `end_`.
2. `try_consume()` returns `false`.
3. `operator++()` executes `value_ = *buf_->ptr_;` which evaluates `*buf_->end_`, dereferencing the one-past-the-end address. If the input is not null-terminated and is located at a page boundary, this causes a segmentation fault or reads out-of-bounds heap/stack memory.
